_doc: the SOURCE OF TRUTH for least-privilege tool grants across all 19 Forge agent-md files (`.claude/agents/*.md`). This file is not documentation-only: `forge-doctor.cjs`'s `agents` check loads it and mechanically compares it against every agent-md's real frontmatter `tools:` line via `forge-policy.cjs`'s `toolPolicyCheck()`. Any drift (an agent gaining a tool not listed here, an agent missing from this file, a policy entry with no matching agent-md, or a class's own forbidden tool showing up in an agent's allowed list) fails forge-doctor and forge-bench. Change tool grants HERE first, keep them in sync with the real agent-md, then re-run forge-doctor. 2026-09-26 (laptop re-audit D1): PowerShell was added next to Bash everywhere Bash is granted — on a Windows host with no bash installed, Claude Code's shell tool IS PowerShell, so a Bash-only grant left every executing Boss unable to run a shell at all. 2026-10-06 (GOAT model routing): each agent's `model` here is its DEFAULT GOAT route model and must equal the agent-md frontmatter `model:` and agent-model-map.json `claudeTier` (routes and values: FORGE_MODEL_ROUTING.json → routes). Only `model` changed in that pass; tools and classes are untouched.
_wp15_note: WP 1.5 (2026-10-24): LEGACY MIRROR. The agent .md frontmatter is now the single source of truth for every per-agent fact; .claude/config/agents/agents.generated.json is generated from it (node .claude/forge-bin/forge-registry-gen.cjs agents --write) and forge-doctor `agents` cross-checks this file against it. This file stays, kept consistent, until a later wave removes it: change the agent frontmatter first, then this mirror, then regenerate. Cross-checked here: each agent's class must equal the class its frontmatter tools give, and no effective tool may be one its class forbids. The class definitions (tools, forbidden) below remain the class policy itself.
bash_is_a_write_primitive_note: Bash is a write-AND-execute primitive, not a read primitive. An agent holding Bash can create, overwrite, or delete any file it can reach (`echo >`, `rm`, a redirect), run `git`/`npm`/`curl`, and invoke arbitrary other programs — REGARDLESS of whether that same agent also has the Write/Edit tool grant. Consequently: (1) an agent with Bash is NEVER meaningfully read-only, even if Write/Edit are absent from its `tools:` line — do not 'harden' an agent by deleting Write/Edit while leaving Bash in place, that removes a convenience API but leaves the exact same blast radius reachable through the shell; (2) the only class in this policy that grants Bash without Write/Edit is `exec-reviewer` (codex-reviewer, verify-boss and scribe), and it is explicitly documented below as a deliberate, narrow, non-read-only exception, never treated as read-only in any report or dashboard panel.
powershell_is_a_write_primitive_note: PowerShell is Claude Code's Windows shell tool (no bash on a fresh Windows install) and is exactly as much a write-AND-execute primitive as Bash — `Set-Content`/`Add-Content`/`Remove-Item`/`Invoke-Expression` reach the same blast radius as `echo >`/`rm`/a pipe-to-shell. Every place this policy grants or forbids Bash grants or forbids PowerShell identically; the two are treated as one shell-execution capability, never as a loophole to grant one while forbidding the other.

read-only-audit.description: Read/search/fetch only. Mechanically cannot change a single file or execute any command (Bash or PowerShell) — the entire value of these roles is an independent, untamperable view of the real repo (and, for research roles, the public web). Used for: review-boss, security-boss, search-boss, seo-boss.

write-no-exec.description: Can read and write/edit files (plans, work packages, docs, JSON registries) but cannot run any command (Bash or PowerShell) — no git, npm, curl, rm, or ad-hoc node/PowerShell scripts. Used for coordination/writing roles whose output is an artifact for another agent (Build Boss, Test Boss, etc.) to actually execute or ship, never something this role executes itself. Used for: boss, head-chef, docs-boss, skill-boss.

full-build.description: Full read/write/execute power — the largest blast radius in the roster. Reserved for roles whose actual job is impossible without running a build, test runner, installer, or other shell tooling (Bash on macOS/Linux/Git-Bash, PowerShell on a Windows host with no bash). Used for: build-boss, test-boss, ui-boss, integration-boss, data-scientist, electron-pro, mcp-developer, ml-engineer, payment-integration.

exec-reviewer.description: Has Bash/PowerShell but not Write/Edit. IMPORTANT: this is NOT a read-only class (see bash_is_a_write_primitive_note/powershell_is_a_write_primitive_note above) — it is a deliberate, narrow exception for a role whose only actual need is invoking an external CLI/slash-command (the Codex plugin) or re-running a build/test command via a shell, with no first-party need to edit repository files through the Write/Edit tool APIs itself. Used for: codex-reviewer, verify-boss, scribe and scribe-acker (scribe and scribe-acker: Bash only, to run forge-scribe.cjs).

boss.rationale: Lead agent: splits the mission into work packages, tracks progress, and receives QA-failure reports — all written to project markdown/JSON (memory, task history, agent ledger). Never itself needs to run a build/test/git command; Build Boss/Test Boss/Integration Boss execute, Boss coordinates and writes plans. No Bash needed or granted.

head-chef.rationale: Converts Boss's mission into exact work packages and verifies subagent completion by reading diffs/reports and writing the work-package docs themselves. No step in its role requires executing a shell command — dispatch and verification are read/write-only. No Bash needed or granted.

review-boss.rationale: Final QA gate: reviews finished work against the user's goal (design, code quality, logic, security, tests, UX, edge cases). Its entire value depends on being unable to alter what it is reviewing — a reviewer that could also write/execute could silently 'fix' the very evidence it is supposed to judge. Read/Grep/Glob only; no Write/Edit/Bash.

test-boss.rationale: Runs real automated tests (Playwright e2e, or the correct strategy per project type) and must write test files/fixtures. Running a real test suite is impossible without a shell (spawning the test runner) — Bash where available, PowerShell on a bash-less Windows host. Full-build is the minimum viable grant for this role.

ui-boss.rationale: Builds and fixes UI/UX, runs real screenshot loops across mobile/tablet/desktop, and needs to launch dev servers/screenshot tooling — none of which is reachable without a shell (Bash, or PowerShell on a bash-less Windows host). Full-build is the minimum viable grant.

seo-boss.rationale: Checks metadata, structure, performance, accessibility, schema, and indexability and reports real findings — an audit/reporting role, not an implementer (fixes go back to Build/UI Boss). WebSearch/WebFetch are needed for CWV/SEO reference lookups. No Write/Edit/Bash — cannot silently 'fix' its own findings.

security-boss.rationale: Explicitly a read-only audit of keys, env vars, auth, webhooks, input validation, and exposed secrets. A security auditor that could also write/execute would be able to alter the evidence of its own findings and would defeat the entire point of an independent audit. Read/Grep/Glob only.

skill-boss.rationale: Maintains the global skill registry and agent-skill bundles by reading/writing JSON config (config/skills/global-skills.json, agent-skill-map.json). Its own body describes only read/validate/write steps (registry checks, bundle attachment, fallback reporting) — no step requires running a shell command. Bash removed 2026-07-14 (was present in frontmatter but unused by the role; write-no-exec is the correct minimum).

search-boss.rationale: Research/current-information role: uses approved search/fetch tools to find sourced facts, never edits the codebase itself. WebSearch/WebFetch are its core function; Write/Edit/Bash would let it silently fabricate 'sourced' content into files instead of reporting findings for another Boss to act on.

build-boss.rationale: Implementation/coding Boss: writes the actual code changes and must run the project's real build/lint/typecheck/test commands to self-review before handoff (per its own checklist). A shell (Bash, or PowerShell on a bash-less Windows host) is core to the role, not incidental.

integration-boss.rationale: Wires APIs, n8n, webhooks, databases, and NVIDIA-as-tool integrations — needs to run install/validate commands (e.g. n8n `validate_workflow`, package installs, curl-based smoke tests) that only a shell (Bash, or PowerShell on a bash-less Windows host) provides.

docs-boss.rationale: Writes docs, setup instructions, and final reports in simple language with exact commands — a pure documentation/handoff role. Its own body (When invoked / checklists) never runs a command itself; it documents commands that Build Boss/Test Boss already ran and verified. Bash removed 2026-07-14 (frontmatter carried it, but nothing in the role needs to execute anything) — cheap haiku model + write-no-exec matches the role's real scope.

data-scientist.rationale: EDA-to-model work requires running real analysis/training scripts and validation harnesses — a shell (Bash, or PowerShell on a bash-less Windows host) is required to execute them, not just author code.

electron-pro.rationale: Builds/hardens an Electron desktop app and must produce a real signed installer/build — packaging tooling only runs through a shell (Bash, or PowerShell on a bash-less Windows host).

mcp-developer.rationale: Builds/debugs MCP servers/clients and must actually run them (JSON-RPC compliance checks, local server smoke tests) — a shell (Bash, or PowerShell on a bash-less Windows host) is required to execute a server process, not optional.

ml-engineer.rationale: Training-to-serving ML pipelines require running real training/eval/deploy scripts to verify reproducibility and drift monitoring — a shell (Bash, or PowerShell on a bash-less Windows host) is core to the role.

payment-integration.rationale: Stripe/gateway integration work needs to run webhook verification tooling and local test-mode charge/refund smoke tests — a shell (Bash, or PowerShell on a bash-less Windows host) is required to execute those checks, not just to author the integration code.

codex-reviewer.rationale: Optional independent code-quality reviewer. Needs a shell (Bash, or PowerShell on a bash-less Windows host) solely to invoke the Codex CLI/slash-commands (`/codex:review`, `/codex:adversarial-review`) and to run `git diff`. Deliberately has NO Write/Edit — it must never directly edit the code it is reviewing. Per bash_is_a_write_primitive/powershell_is_a_write_primitive, this agent is NOT read-only despite lacking Write/Edit; it is classified exec-reviewer, a distinct, narrower-than-full-build class than a coder role, not a security-equivalent to review-boss/security-boss.

verify-boss.rationale: DEFAULT verifier per work package (GOAT routing 2026-10-06; sonnet/medium; replies PASS/FAIL with evidence, never edits) and independent RE-EXECUTOR: re-runs the exact build/test/health-check command a Boss claims passed, from a cold read of the diff, and reports the literal exit code. Needs a shell (Bash, or PowerShell on a bash-less Windows host) to actually re-execute those checks (forge-doctor/forge-runwatch/forge-flaky/the cited test suite) — a re-executor that could not run a command would be pointless. Deliberately has NO Write/Edit — per bash_is_a_write_primitive/powershell_is_a_write_primitive it is NOT read-only, but it must never be able to 'fix' the very evidence it verifies, so exec-reviewer (Bash/PowerShell + Read/Grep/Glob, no Write/Edit) is the correct minimum. Distinct from codex-reviewer (external Codex opinion) and from read-only review-boss/security-boss (which cannot re-execute at all).

scribe.rationale: Owner-requirements ledger keeper (GOAT quick route sonnet/low). Needs Bash solely to run `node .claude/forge-bin/forge-scribe.cjs` — the ONLY sanctioned way to change scribe state (capture/classify/link/transition/gate/digest) — plus read-only inspection. Deliberately has NO Write/Edit so it can never hand-edit the inbox/ledger or any project file. Per bash_is_a_write_primitive it is NOT read-only; exec-reviewer is the correct minimum. No PowerShell: forge-scribe.cjs is a plain node CLI that Bash (Git Bash on Windows) runs.

scribe-acker.rationale: Owner-delegated acceptor (R-0233, GOAT quick route sonnet/low). Needs Bash solely to run `node .claude/forge-bin/forge-scribe.cjs autoack` (and read-only gate/list), which decides every accept or hold itself. Deliberately has NO Write/Edit so it can never hand-edit the inbox/ledger or any project file, and no PowerShell (a plain node CLI). Per bash_is_a_write_primitive it is NOT read-only; exec-reviewer is the correct minimum, like scribe.
